correctness.rationale: For t=2^a>=4, p odd prime, S=(t-1)p+2t-1. If D(S)=tp, valuation nu_2(S)=1 makes D(S) odd; valuation >=3 gives D(S)/S>=3/2 and S/n>3/4, contradictory. Thus S=4m odd m, with exact identities p=4D(m)+2t-1 and m-(t-1)D(m)=t(2t-1)/4. Since D(m)=Omega(m) mod2, this forces even Omega for a=2 and odd Omega for a>=3. For Omega<=2 and a>=3, m is prime and the two simultaneous prime formulas follow; conversely these imply D(S)=n. For a=2, Omega=2 gives (r-3)(s-3)=16; pairs (5,11) and (7,7), and only former gives p=71 and n=284. The first case a=3,p=19 has q=37,n=152. Independent factor/derivative calculations over 616 (a,p) pairs corroborated the logic. No assertion for higher Omega, a=1 or infinitely many simultaneous primes.
